bookCover.coverDescription: III.G Sets, Q2 — Items in Exactly One Set

params.text:
Start with examples

Before choosing a set operation, predict a few outputs from the task's rule. Concrete examples give you a result to explain before you plan an algorithm.

III.G Q2 · Sets

Notebook task

  • Write xor(first, second).
  • Accept two sets and return a set of the items that are in one set or the other, but not both.

Learning goals

  • Classify items by membership in two sets.
  • Compare familiar set operations with the target result.
  • Test a rule on varied input pairs before coding.

Work with a partner. Before you choose an answer, write down what you think will happen. Tell your partner why. Your partner can try an example to check your idea. Switch roles on each page. Select Check to get feedback. If you need another try, select Retry. At the end, write your own function in the course notebook.

On paper, start with first = {"a", "b", "c"} and second = {"b", "d"}. List the candidate items, then predict the returned set. Focus on which items are present, not on the order in which Python might display them.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Yes. Each of these items occurs in exactly one input; b occurs in both.
This includes b, which occurs in both inputs. Recheck the last part of the task rule.
This keeps only the shared item. The task asks for items in one input but not both.

params.question:
Check the predicted members

For first = {"a", "b", "c"} and second = {"b", "d"}, which set contains exactly the items that xor(first, second) should return?

answers.text: The result can still be correct if it has the same members.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Set equality depends on membership, not display order.

answers.text: The result is wrong unless its display order matches the first input.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A set does not preserve the first input as an answer order. Compare members instead.

answers.text: The result must always be sorted alphabetically.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Sets do not promise an alphabetical display order.

params.question:
A member of both inputs

For first = {"a", "b", "c"} and second = {"b", "d"}, what should happen to "b" in the returned set?

answers.text: Leave it out because it occurs in neither input.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. An output member must come from one of the input sets.

answers.text: Include it because it does not occur in both inputs.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: “Not both” alone is not enough: the item must occur in one input.
Sets contain actual items. There is no placeholder item for a value that never appeared.

params.text:
Fill in a flowchart

With the membership decisions in view, compare familiar set operations on the same inputs. This lets you check which information each operation keeps before combining ideas.

Return to first = {"a", "b", "c"} and second = {"b", "d"}. Copy this flowchart onto paper. Fill each blank with union, intersection, or difference. Both branches begin with the original input sets.

Two branches followed by one final step
Branch 1: all candidate itemsBranch 2: shared items
first and second
↓
Operation: ____
↓
Call the result U		first and second
↓
Operation: ____
↓
Call the result I
↓ Use the two branch results in this order: ____ then ____
Final operation: ____
Remove the shared items from the broader collection.

Predict the members of U, I, and the final result before using Check. The final step must happen after both branches, so the inputs to that step are the two intermediate sets.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The union contains every item found in either input. Compare it with the target set.
That is only the shared item. Union includes items found in either input.
This leaves out the shared item. Union includes b as well.

Order the final step

Let U = first.union(second) and I = first.intersection(second). Which expression removes the shared items while retaining items unique to either input?

If no items qualify, write the Python value for an empty set. Compare that value with an empty dictionary or list.
